draft.title: Winning the war
card: The Continental Army, led by George Washington, fought the British army and navy for years. It was often short of money, food and supplies.
France joined the war on the American side after the American win at Saratoga in 1777. It sent money, soldiers, and a navy.
In 1781 a French fleet blocked the sea route at Yorktown, Virginia. British general Cornwallis was trapped by American and French armies and surrendered.
Britain then agreed to peace. In the Treaty of Paris in 1783, it recognised the United States as an independent nation.
draft.remember: French help, especially at Yorktown, let the Americans win, and Britain accepted independence in 1783.

a.q: Why was French help so important at Yorktown in 1781?
opts: Its fleet cut off the sea route, trapping Cornwallis
Its fleet destroyed the British army in Boston
Its army took over command from Washington
Its king paid the Continental Army to end the war
a.why: The French fleet blocked escape and supply by sea, while American and French armies surrounded Cornwallis on land. He was trapped and surrendered. French soldiers fought there, but they did not replace Washington as leader.
a.clue: Think about how the French navy stopped the British from leaving.

b.q: Which event in 1783 ended the war and gave Britain's formal recognition of American independence?
opts: The Treaty of Paris
The surrender at Yorktown
The battle of Saratoga
The French alliance
b.why: In the Treaty of Paris, Britain formally recognised the United States as independent. Yorktown in 1781 was the last major surrender, but it did not itself set out the terms of peace.
b.clue: Which event was an agreement between governments, not a battle?

a.best: Its fleet cut off the sea route, trapping Cornwallis

a.q: Why was French help so important at Yorktown in 1781?
opts: Its fleet blocked the sea, so Cornwallis could not escape
Its fleet carried Washington's army north to New York
Its fleet attacked Britain's coast to force a peace
Its army took over command from Washington
a.why: The French fleet blocked the sea route, while American and French armies surrounded Cornwallis on land. With no way out by sea, he was trapped and surrendered. The fleet's work was at Yorktown itself, not along Britain's coast or in New York.
a.clue: Where was Cornwallis when he surrendered?

b.q: Which event in 1783 ended the war and gave Britain's formal recognition of American independence?
opts: The Treaty of Paris
The surrender at Yorktown
The battle of Saratoga
The French alliance
b.why: In the Treaty of Paris, Britain formally recognised the United States as independent. Yorktown in 1781 was the last major surrender, but it did not itself set out the terms of peace.
b.clue: Which event was an agreement between governments, not a battle?

a.best: Its fleet blocked the sea, so Cornwallis could not escape
